articles.headline: Premier League live updates: Chelsea host Spurs, City lose unbeaten record to Villa
articles.description: Chelsea take on Tottenham as Arsenal move joint-top of the Premier League following Man City's defeat to Aston Villa, with another busy weekend of European soccer continuing.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ速報：チェルシーがスパーズを迎え撃つ、シティはヴィラに敗れ無敗記録がストップ
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティがアストン・ヴィラに敗れ、アーセナルがプレミアリーグの首位に並ぶ中、チェルシー対トッテナムの一戦が行われる。欧州サッカーの熱い週末が続く。
articles.body:
We're back with another action-packed weekend of European soccer!

In the Premier League, Aston Villa kept up their recent success at home over Manchester City to win 2-1 and end City's 100% start to the season.

Defending champions Arsenal hosted Everton at the Emirates Stadium looking to go level at the top of the table and did so after a 2-0 win, while Coventry City took on Fulham at the same time, only for the visitors to end up as 1-0 winners.

Later, we wrap up the Premier League slate with a London derby, as Xabi Alonso's Chelsea face Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge.

Elsewhere, Arsenal's women beat rivals Spurs 2-1 in the WSL, Napoli host AS Roma in a huge Serie A showdown, while Borussia Dortmund welcome Eintracht Frankfurt to Signal Iduna Park.

Enjoy all the action from Saturday's matches across Europe.

articles.headline: Sources: Magic's Banchero out multiple weeks with low-grade high ankle sprain
articles.description: Magic star Paolo Banchero sustained a low-grade high ankle sprain and will miss multiple weeks, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：マジックのバンチェロ、軽度の足関節高位捻挫で数週間の離脱
articles.descriptionJa: マジックのスター、パオロ・バンチェロが軽度の足関節高位捻挫を負い、数週間の欠場となる見込みであることが、ESPNのシャムス・チャラニア氏への情報筋の取材で判明した。
articles.body:
Orlando Magic star Paolo Banchero sustained a low-grade high ankle sprain and will miss multiple weeks, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

This injury diagnosis typically carries a timetable of four to six weeks.

Banchero was injured in the third quarter of Friday night's 115-93 loss to the visiting Timberwolves. He sat out the fourth quarter and finished with 14 points and six rebounds.

Last season, the Magic outscored opponents by 45 points in the 182 minutes Banchero, Franz Wagner, Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane and Wendell Carter Jr. were on the court together. They collectively shot 50.1% from the field and 36.4% from 3-point range, while holding opponents to just 46.2% overall shooting and 34.5% 3-point shooting.

The Magic are 40-26 over the last three regular seasons when the quartet of Banchero, Wagner, Suggs and Carter all play, for a 60.6% winning percentage.

The last two seasons combined, Banchero missed 46 games, Wagner 70 and Suggs 72, yet the Magic still reached the playoffs both years.

articles.headline: Arise Arsenal, the people's Premier League champions
articles.description: The sight of Man City pulling clear at the top of the Premier League table was not a good look for the biggest league in the world. But Arsenal's win against Everton showed they are ready to fight all the way this season.
articles.headlineJa: アーセナルの台頭、民衆のプレミアリーグ王者へ
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグの首位を独走する姿は、世界最大のリーグにとって決して良い光景ではなかった。しかし、アーセナルのエヴァートン戦での勝利は、今シーズン最後まで戦い抜く準備ができていることを示した。
articles.body:
LONDON -- Winners usually become unpopular pretty quickly because everybody wants to see the best knocked off their perch, but after capitalizing on Manchester City's first defeat of the season to move level on points with the Premier League leaders, Arsenal proved they can be people's champions as well as Premier League champions.

A routine 2-0 home win against Everton thanks to goals from defenders Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães in each half enabled the Gunners to close a three-point gap on City to just goal difference, following Aston Villa's 2-1 win against Enzo Maresca's side earlier in the day.

Who knows if we are in for an epic title race or an Arsenal procession due to the uncertainty surrounding City and the outcome of their appeal against the guilty verdict in their case against the Premier League? If their appeal is thrown out, City could be relegated rather than title winners.

"We have to just focus on what we can do," Arteta said when asked about the strange situation of battling with City at the top. "We are very pleased with 90% of our result and performances other than the Brighton game [3-0 defeat last month]."

It is too early in the season to talk of runaway leaders, but City had been looking formidable prior to their slip at Villa Park following seven straight league wins and that was becoming kind of awkward for the Premier League.

With an independent commission finding the club guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules last month -- City, who have lodged an appeal, were found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges -- the sight of Maresca's side pulling clear at the top of the table was not a good look for the biggest league in the world.

Just imagine the scenes at the end of the season if the disciplinary process is still unresolved and the Premier League trophy is held aloft with light blue ribbons at the Etihad.

Awkward is an understatement, especially if City have to hand the trophy back days or weeks later because of, in the words of Premier League CEO Richard Masters, "systematically breaking Premier League rules for nearly a decade."

That nightmare scenario might still happen, but Arsenal's win against Everton showed they are ready to fight City all the way this season. Arteta's side are defending champions and are desperate to retain their title.

When they won the title last season -- Arsenal's first since 2003-04 -- Arteta's team were anything but universally popular champions. Their style of play, overreliance on set-pieces and readiness to waste time, plus Arteta's touchline antics, had many rival fans hoping for yet another City title. But that animosity towards Arsenal has gone because of the reaction to City being found guilty of breaking so many rules.

When they returned to action with a 3-0 win at Liverpool earlier this month after being hit with the guilty verdict during the international break, City were subjected to chants of "cheats" and greeted with ban

articles.headline: NFL Week 7 uniforms: Alternates galore as Texans go battle red, Lions all-black
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 7, led by alternate looks from Houston, Detroit and Dallas.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第7週のユニフォーム：テキサンズの赤、ライオンズのオールブラックなど、多彩なオルタネートが登場
articles.descriptionJa: ヒューストン、デトロイト、ダラスのオルタネート（特別仕様）ユニフォームを中心に、NFL各チームの第7週の着用ウェアを紹介する。
articles.body:
The throwbacks were well-represented in Week 6 of the NFL slate. While that's still the case this week, it's the alternates that lead the way -- including two monochromatic looks from the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions.

Houston will be wearing its "battle red" combination, which the team first unveiled in 2024. It's all red from head to toe complete with a similarly colored matte lid that includes a new bullhorn logo. The numbers are deep steel blue with a liberty white trim, while the red pants boast blue and white stripes. The New York Giants will counter with all-white. 

Also unveiled in 2024, the Lions are rocking their all-black threads against the Green Bay Packers. The black jersey and pants include a Honolulu Blue matte helmet with leaping Lions logo in silver. There's also a black stripe across the middle. Detroit first wore black uniforms in 1948 before bringing it back in 2005 as an alternate. The team stopped wearing them after the 2007 season before returning it in 2024. 

The Dallas Cowboys will don their color rush look against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." Dallas unveiled these threads in 2015 with a silver helmet before an arctic white one debuted in 2022. The all-white combination has navy blue numbers and on the shoulder for a neat look.

Though alternates are the headliners, fans of the classics aren't leaving empty handed either in Week 7.

The Seattle Seahawks are wearing their throwbacks from the 1990s, complete with royal blue jerseys and silver pants and helmet. Seattle wore them last week on "Thursday Night Football." For the first time this season, the Atlanta Falcons and New York Jets are rocking classic uniforms. New York's is appropriately named "The Classic," and the all-white look pays homage to the 1968 championship season. It also includes uniform details from 1998 to 2018. Atlanta's threads include its iconic red helmet, which dates back to the 1960s, with black jerseys and white pants. 

The first NFL game in Paris brings a first in the uniform department for the Pittsburgh Steelers. Pittsburgh will rock their traditional white jerseys, but with color rush black pants, creating a combination never seen before for the franchise. The Steelers typically wear gold pants home or away. But, it will be a different look against the New Orleans Saints.

articles.headline: Man City lose 100% Premier League record with defeat at Aston Villa
articles.description: Manchester City suffered defeat for the first time in the Premier League this season when Nicolas Jackson's double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ、アストン・ヴィラに敗れプレミアリーグ全勝記録が途絶える
articles.descriptionJa: ニコラス・ジャクソンが2ゴールを挙げたアストン・ヴィラに1-2で敗れ、マンチェスター・シティは今シーズンのプレミアリーグで初めての黒星を喫した。
articles.body:
Manchester City suffered defeat for the first time in the Premier League this season when Nicolas Jackson's double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park.

Unai Emery's side continued its turnaround in form after a slow start to the campaign and picked up a fourth straight win across all competitions, and its first league victory at home this season.

Manchester City do not enjoy visiting Villa Park and have now lost their last four league games there, while Enzo Maresca saw his 100% league start as City boss vanish.

Another tough afternoon in the West Midlands started when Marc Guéhi's mistake allowed Jackson to give Villa an early lead.

Villa had keeper Zion Suzuki to thank for making several vital saves, and Iliman Ndiaye crashed an effort off the post as Villa held strong to take the lead into the break.

Erling Haaland grabbed his ninth league goal of the season to get City level, but Jackson buried his second of the afternoon -- his fourth of the season -- on the hour mark to hand Villa the points.

The visitors were greeted with more boos from an away ground ahead of kickoff after they were found guilty of serious breaches of the competition's financial regulations last month.

City conceded a corner after Gianluigi Donnarumma took too long to take his goal kick, which put City on the back foot, and Villa's quick start was rewarded with the opener in the sixth minute.

Guéhi was unable to control the ball and instead spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it into Jackson, and he expertly finished into the top of the net.

The early goal did not dent City's confidence, and they were denied an equalizer when Suzuki sprang right to push Ndiaye's curling effort away.

The Japan goalkeeper was getting busier by the minute. He put out an outstretched arm to thwart Rayan Cherki following some neat footwork by Jérémy Doku before stopping Abdukodir Khusanov from range.

Ndiaye had already threatened Suzuki once by cutting inside and letting one rip, and he did it again, only to see the effort slam off the outside of the post.

Haaland had a quiet first half but made his contribution seven minutes after the break to get City level when he nodded Ndiaye's cross past Suzuki.

City's onslaught continued and Villa's woodwork was rattled again; this time Suzuki tipped Josko Gvardiol's ferocious strike off the bar.

And that save proved decisive as Villa retook the lead just as it looked like City were turning up the heat on the hour mark.

articles.headline: Marc Guéhi form doesn't worry Man City boss Enzo Maresca despite errors
articles.description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is not worried by the form of defender Marc Guéhi after his mistake contributed to their 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa.
articles.headlineJa: マン市のエンツォ・マレスカ監督、ミスをしたマルク・ゲヒの状態に不安なし
articles.descriptionJa: アストン・ヴィラ戦の1-2の敗戦に影響したミスがあったものの、マンチェスター・シティのエンツォ・マレスカ監督はディフェンダーのマルク・ゲヒの状態について懸念していない。
articles.body:
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is not worried by the form of defender Marc Guéhi after his mistake contributed to their 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa.

Guehi mis-controlled a high ball out from the back which allowed Nicolas Jackson to give Villa a half-time lead.

Erling Haaland nodded in his ninth league goal of the campaign to get City level but Jackson had the final say when he scored for a second time to hand Villa the points.

Guehi has been under the spotlight following a series of high-profile errors that have led to goals recently, and after also receiving a yellow card in the first half, he was substituted at the break.

He made a critical early mistake that helped gift Spain a win over England during the international break as well as conceding a penalty in last week's win over Ipswich, and Saturday's error added to his recent catalogue.

However, Maresca insists he has no concerns about his central defender's form.

He said: "It's just a technical decision, like it happens in all the games that the manager decides to make a change.

"I'm not worried about Marc at all. I know that he is playing every minute since the season started with us and with the international team.

"It's not easy but the change was also because he had a yellow card, and the way we want to be aggressive sometimes, to have one yellow card can be dangerous. But I'm not worried at all."

Maresca's 100% start to life as City boss in the league came to an end which means they have now lost the last four times at Villa Park.

However, Maresca felt his side should have come away with something from the match.

He added: "I think we deserved more from the game, for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances that we conceded.

"We lost because we were probably not being clinical enough in their box. Sometimes when you concede the first goal because of a mistake. The second goal came from a transition, it's difficult to avoid.

- Man City beaten by double from Aston Villa's Jackson

"We will try to learn from the game, move on and try to improve.

"We need to find that balance. Second half I don't remember any more shots or any more chances for them apart from the goal we conceded in transition."

Aston Villa have put their slow start to the season behind them and the win over City brought them a sixth win from seven in all competitions.

Boss Unai Emery believes his side's recent upturn in form is due to the time his squad needed to adapt to his style.

He said: "Manchester City are the best team in the league, until now. They are one of the best teams in the world.

"This is the level we were last year and getting the levels close with those teams.

"This year we started poor. We needed time to understand better how we need to improve and work individually and tactically.

"Today this test was a good test and we responded. The players showed us the capacity to recover the level of last year. This is a good example of how we are progressing."

articles.headline: Fulham out of relegation zone by beating Coventry
articles.description: Oscar Bobb's first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.
articles.headlineJa: フルアム、コヴェントリーに勝利し降格圏を脱出
articles.descriptionJa: オスカー・ボブがフルアム加入後プレミアリーグ初ゴールを決め、コヴェントリーに1-0で勝利。これによりフルアムは降格圏から脱出した。
articles.body:
Oscar Bobb's first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27 million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard's side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham's half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Quality was in short supply between two sides who started the day in the bottom three.

King should have broken the deadlock in the 18th minute when afforded too much space in the box, but his powerful strike rebounded off the top of the upright before Alex Iwobi sent a wild follow-up effort high and wide.

At the other end, Bobby Thomas met Rudoni's free-kick but got his angles all wrong as he headed well wide, before Brandon Thomas-Asante headed wide from Jay Dasilva's cross following a good run forward from Rudoni.

A mis-hit backpass from Antonee Robinson offered Thomas-Asante another chance but his shot lacked power as Leno easily gathered.

While Coventry were piling up half-chances Fulham were the ones bossing possession but, in keeping with their season so far, struggling to turn that sort of dominance into goals.

Coventry defender Milan van Ewijk almost helped them out, deflecting Robinson's low cross dangerously close to his own goal as it found the side-netting.

Just before the break, Calvin Bassey went down in the box claiming a shirt-pull from Thomas-Asante, but referee Adam Herczeg waved play on with replays suggesting they each had a hold of the other.

VAR had taken a look, and was involved again early in the second half when Rudoni's free-kick from the right struck Iwobi on the arm before he cleared, but the Nigerian's arms were by his side and play was waved on.

Coventry then suffered a major blow when the in-form Thomas, praised by Frank Lampard in midweek, hobbled off just before the hour, replaced by teenage Manchester City loanee Stephen Mfuni.

The hosts were starting to build some momentum after a series of substitutions but it swiftly ended as Bobb struck with 10 minutes to go.

Coventry tried to respond but a powerful strike from Matt Grimes was blocked and a late penalty appeal for handball against Shea Charles was waved away with the midfielder having had his arm tucked

articles.headlineJa: 土曜日のNBAファンタジーバスケットボール：おすすめの獲得選手とベッティング
articles.descriptionJa: ジム・マコーミックが土曜日の試合日程を分析し、ファンタジーで獲得すべきストリーマーやおすすめの賭け先を解説する。
articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Saturday

This first Saturday of the NBA regular season presents a mix of potential blowouts and battles. Five of Saturday's contests have large point spreads, while three have more competitive betting metrics.

Navigating big lines can prove challenging. Will the coaches abandon rotation patterns in the face of a blowout? A solid approach is to prioritize players whose value does not rely on a full fourth quarter; high-usage stars in competitive games, centers who can reach value through rebounds and blocks early, and starters with secure roles. Big lines still regularly surface from blowouts, as Stephen Curry has taught us over the past 15 years.

Potential blowouts don't automatically eliminate stars or create bench value. They simply add another variable: how much of a player's projection depends on a normal late-game workload. Compare that risk against matchup, injury news and the realistic likelihood the game stays close. The same idea applies to props: a large number is worth weighing, not treating as an automatic under.

Among the games with closer lines, the Miami Heat face the Charlotte Hornets in a game that feels important for Giannis Antetokounmpo and this new-look roster to prove competitive after a slow start. Conversely, Charlotte got drubbed last night by the Atlanta Hawks, setting up two division foes seeking redemption.

Speaking of the Hawks, they host the Houston Rockets in the marquee matchup of the day. These cross-conference teams boast deep rosters with gifted defenders, setting up an anticipated matchup for this initial weekend of the season.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team -- widely available players worth adding

Davion Mitchell, PG, Miami Heat (rostered in 23.5% of ESPN leagues)

The Heat simply need more creation and scoring to complement Giannis and Bam Adebayo. Mitchell, thus far, has assumed more deliberate distribution duties for Miami versus last year's track meet agenda. With a strong floor for assists and steals and growing upside as a 3-point threat, Mitchell makes the cut as a top guard to consider today. It also helps that Charlotte is running a patchworked point guard rotation.

Naji Marshall, SF/PF, Dallas Mavericks (15.4%)

After proving himself as a steady bucket throughout last spring, Marshall is the clear favorite to assume heavy usage with Cooper Flagg likely sidelined with a shoulder injury suffered last night against the Indiana Pacers. Welcome to The Playbook for Week 7, which kicked off Thursday night with a game between the Patriots and Bears.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start advice, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday after 1 p.m. ET. 

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 7
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Patriots-Bears game.

Teams on bye in Week 7: Bills, Chargers, Commanders, Jaguars

Week 7 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 vs GB

He scored 17.7 fantasy points in his worst game this season. Week 7 will not be his worst game. 
 2. Ja'Marr Chase, WR1 @ BAL

 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR2 vs KC

 4. Kenneth Walker III, RB2 @ SEA

He spent four seasons in Seattle. This is a revenge game. Then again, it has been a revenge season for him.
 5. Christian McCaffrey, RB3 @ ATL

Season-high volume after Mike Evans left Monday. Be careful what you wish for, investors.
 6. Brock Purdy, QB1 @ ATL

Naysayers can point to three consecutive games with fewer than 20 points. We're not naysayers here.
 7. Jordan Love, QB2 @ DET

 8. Bijan Robinson, RB4 vs SF

How does this fellow get only 11 touches in a football game? The Falcons must do better this week.
 9. Derrick Henry, RB5 vs CIN

 10. Kyren Williams, RB6 @ LV

Perhaps the loss of Davante Adams pushes the Rams to run more. The current plan is not working.
 11. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR3 vs GB

No trepidation here, but he really has not lit up the Packers in recent seasons. 
 12. Justin Jefferson, WR4 vs IND

 13. CeeDee Lamb, WR5 @ PHI

 14. Brock Bowers, TE1 vs LAR

His targets have dropped each of the past three weeks. Expect that streak to end this week.
 15. Lamar Jackson, QB3 vs CIN

 16. Joe Burrow, QB4 @ BAL

 17. C.J. Stroud, QB5 vs NYG

Nobody thought he would have the fifth-most points among QBs. It looks legit, though.
 18. Jared Goff, QB6 vs GB

 19. Matthew Stafford, QB7 @ LV

Nobody is throwing more than he is, but losing Adams is a really big deal. 
 20. Malik Nabers, WR6 @ HOU

articles.headline: Ex-NBA player Malik Beasley negotiating plea deal in gambling case
articles.description: Former NBA player Malik Beasley is negotiating a plea agreement with Department of Justice lawyers over his alleged role in a bribery and betting scheme, one of his attorneys confirmed.
articles.headlineJa: 元NBAのマリク・ビーズリー、賭博事件で司法取引を交渉中
articles.descriptionJa: 元NBA選手のマリク・ビーズリーが、贈収賄および賭博スキームへの関与の疑いを巡り、司法省の検察官と司法取引の交渉を行っていることが、弁護士の一人によって確認された。
articles.body:
Former NBA player Malik Beasley is negotiating a plea agreement with Department of Justice lawyers over his alleged role in a bribery and betting scheme, one of his attorneys confirmed Saturday.

An overnight notice on the court docket indicated that Beasley, who played for six NBA teams over a nine-year career, intends to plead guilty in the case. Attorney Steve Haney told ESPN in a text message that Beasley has not signed a plea deal with prosecutors but that talks are ongoing and a decision is expected early this week.

A spokesperson for the Eastern District of New York did not immediately reply to follow-up questions about the matter.

Prosecutors allege that Beasley, 29, deliberately manipulated his statistics in at least four games during the 2023-24 season while he was with the Milwaukee Bucks so that gamblers could place and win bets on his performances.

According to the indictment, his co-defendants selected games that would not be nationally televised and Beasley decided whether he would underperform or overperform his scoring and rebounding.

Though he had earned tens of millions of dollars during his career, Beasley also accumulated "multimillion-dollar gambling losses" when he became part of the alleged scheme, according to the indictment.

Beasley faces federal counts of bribery in sporting contests, wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy and money laundering conspiracy. He initially pleaded not guilty to all of the charges.

Late Friday, however, the judge overseeing his case asked a federal magistrate in Brooklyn to schedule a hearing for Beasley to change his plea. The judge filed a similar order Friday for another defendant in the case, Ernesto Plascencia. Plascencia's attorney confirmed Saturday morning that he will be entering a guilty plea.

One of the other defendants in the case, William Brown, pleaded guilty earlier this month, while fellow sports bettor Robert Gorodetsky is slated to formally enter a guilty plea Nov. 20.

Former NBA player Ed Davis and Paolo Zamorano, who was Davis' agent, were also charged in the case and have pleaded not guilty.

ABC News contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Amen Thompson stuffs Wembanyama's last-second shot as Rockets hold off Spurs
articles.description: Amen Thompson blocked Victor Wembanyama at the rim to prevent a potential tying bucket as the Rockets beat the Spurs 114-110.
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas -- Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson couldn't quite explain what happened after sealing a 114-110 victory over the San Antonio Spurs by swatting away a last-gasp attempt at the rim by Victor Wembanyama.

In the aftermath of the game-saving play, Rockets forward Kevin Durant scurried over in excitement to deliver Thompson a message Friday as the sellout crowd at Moody Center groaned in disbelief.

"I said, 'What the f--- is wrong with him, thinking he was just going to lay it up so easily?'" Durant recalled.

"I don't know," Thompson shot back.

With five seconds remaining and Houston clinging to a 112-110 lead, Spurs point guard De'Aaron Fox floated a pass over Rockets forward Jabari Smith Jr. to Wembanyama, just as the big man spun toward the basket outside the restricted area. Wembanyama soared for what usually ends with a dunk. But Wembanyama's 8-foot wingspan couldn't clear Thompson's 7-foot reach and pogo-stick leaping ability.

"I just knew they were going to try to get probably me or one of the other smaller guys on him," Thompson said. "I jump pretty high, so I wouldn't try to keep ducking [in on] me."

Thompson smacked Wembanyama's attempt into the waiting hands of Fred VanVleet, who iced the game with a pair of free throws.

"Man, what an incredible block," Durant said. "It was just insane, man. As soon as your feet hit the ground, to be able to bounce back up so quick, that's rare in any human. To be 6-7, dunk the ball and block shots like a center is insane."

Thompson finished with a team-worst minus-12 on the box score. But what transpired on the floor told a different story for the 23-year-old, who finished with 20 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, two blocks and a pair of steals.

"We did a really good job of switching and denying some catches, pushed [Wembanyama] off his spot, did his work early instead of getting ducked in like we did quite a few times," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said. "And from there, he uses athleticism and God-given ability there and did a hell of a job one-on-one with him in the post."

Thompson worked Wembanyama on the offensive end too. With 1:13 left in the third quarter, Thompson cut to the basket for a two-hand jam over the Frenchman off an assist by Durant. Wembanyama fouled Thompson on the play, and the Rockets guard nailed the and-1 free throw to give Houston a nine-point lead.

"That's low-key getting dunked on, right?" Thompson said, smiling.

Thompson and Durant scored 20 points apiece, but Rockets center Alperen Sengun dominated Wembanyama and the rest of the Spurs bigs to pour in a game-high 29 points with seven rebounds and seven assists. The performance marked his 35th career game with 25 points, five rebounds and five assists, tying Steve Francis for the second-most such games by a Rockets player before age 25.

Sengun scored 18 points in the second half, including 14 in the fourth quarter, to help Houston get off to its first 2-0 start since 2017-18.
